issue_context.title: v243 breaks lvremove of snapshots
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
> v243

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released systemd versions upstream! -->
<!-- For older version please use distribution trackers (see https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/master/docs/CONTRIBUTING.md#filing-issues). -->

**Used distribution**
 > Gentoo

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
```
# lvcreate -s --size=5116M --name=mysql_snapshot /dev/SQL/mysql
  Logical volume "mysql_snapshot" created.
# lvremove -f /dev/SQL/mysql_snapshot 
  Logical volume "mysql_snapshot" successfully removed
```

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
```
# lvcreate -s --size=5116M --name=mysql_snapshot /dev/SQL/mysql
  Logical volume "mysql_snapshot" created.
# lvremove -f /dev/SQL/mysql_snapshot
```
Here the lvremove hangs and I have to "kill -9" it. Oddly enough a second lvremove then is "successful":
```
# lvremove -f /dev/SQL/mysql_snapshot 
  WARNING: Reading VG SQL from disk because lvmetad metadata is invalid.
  Logical volume "mysql_snapshot" successfully removed
```

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
1. Create a volume group, say SQL.
2. `lvcreate -L 5G -n mysql SQL`
3. `mkfs.ext4 /dev/SQL/mysql`
4. `lvcreate -s --size=5116M --name=mysql_snapshot /dev/SQL/mysql`
5. `lvremove -f /dev/SQL/mysql_snapshot`
6. As this lvremove does not terminate, `kill -9` it.
7. `lvremove -f /dev/SQL/mysql_snapshot`
  `WARNING: Reading VG RAID from disk because lvmetad metadata is invalid.
  Logical volume "mysql_snapshot" successfully removed`


**Workaround**
Downgrade to systemd-242.
comments: Please contact the LVM people about this. We don't know LVM. They'll help you and then report any issue they find back to us. Thank you!

Maybe the underlying "bug" is in the lvm code, but then the changes (probably in the udev code) from systemd-242 to -243 trigger it, as I didn't change anything in the lvm software on the affected host.

Investigating it further I found following lines in the journal just at the time of the lvremove stall:
```
systemd-udevd[2097]: dm-3: Failed to process device, ignoring: No such file or directory
systemd-udevd[2096]: dm-4: Failed to process device, ignoring: No such file or directory
```
On starting the systemd-udevd also states that it is
```
Using default interface naming scheme 'v243'.
```
@protegh If you are familiar with git, you could try to run a `git bisect` to identify the change in systemd which triggered this issue?

> Please test PR #13984.

This fixed it. Thanks!

review_comments: looks good, but what about the operation below? shouldn't they all just fail silently on ENOENT? i.e. the chmod_and_chown() and so on?
Hmm??? On ENOENT, this return with 0, so `chmod_and_chown()` is not called.

well, but what happens if during the lstat() the device is still there, but then during the chmod() it is gone? I mean, we never know when precisely the device disappears, could be any time, hence we should handle it on all operations?

(Alternatively we could of course operate on an open(O_PATH) fd instead, so that removal doesn't invalidate the object for us)
I see. I understand. Now, ENOENT in `chmod_and_chown()` or later operations are also ignored. PTAL.
